title: Eleva design audit and plan
status: Audit of 2026-11-14 with its plan. By 2026-11-21, 18 of the first 39 slices are merged (D0.1 to D0.3, D1.1 to D1.5, D2.1, D2.2, D5.7 to D5.9, D7.1 to D7.5); the 21 still open, and the three of Phase 8, are listed in execution-plan/remaining-roadmap.md. On 2026-11-23 the public site became its own track (Track E, the marketing thread) and the founder opened its whole design for a rethink: Phase 8 holds the new slices, and D3, D2.3, D2.4 and D6.1 are built in that track against the seven-seat panel in judges-panel.md.

topMoves.title: Rebuild the pay step as a confirm-and-pay page, in a quiet checkout frame
topMoves.why: The money moment is the thinnest screen in the product: no price breakdown, nothing reassuring beside the button, and the whole funnel sits inside the marketing header and a forty-link footer.

topMoves.title: Turn the checked registration into visible proof, on the profile and on every expert card
topMoves.why: It is the one fact Eleva verifies about an expert, and today it reads as grey small print.

topMoves.title: Give every profile a person: photo rule, profession line, approach, first session
topMoves.why: A member is choosing someone to trust with her health. Without a photo and a structured story the page is a monogram and a price.

topMoves.title: Put real, bookable experts and a need-first entry on the homepage and the explorer
topMoves.why: The homepage never shows an expert a member can book, and neither page lets her start from what she needs.

topMoves.title: Give experts a door, then rebuild setup as one focused, profile-first journey
topMoves.why: A professional who signs up lands on a member Space with no way in. Setup then opens with a tax number and never shows her the profile she is building.

topMoves.title: Make the two home pages answer a question
topMoves.why: Expert Today should say what needs her today and whether she can be paid. Member home should feel like a companion, not an empty admin panel.

topMoves.title: Explain each trust moment in one plain sentence, where it is asked
topMoves.why: The legal substance is complete, but the health-data consent is a bare link and the privacy page is five identical Grant buttons.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.goal: Make the next phases judgeable: real-looking content, no broken first-run path, and a complete baseline.

slices.title: Realistic demo seed
slices.scope: Seeded experts get portraits, a profession line, real bios and services; the demo member gets one upcoming and one past session with a report. Without this every profile and dashboard design is judged on placeholders.

slices.title: Fix the /onboarding error for accounts that already have a Space
slices.scope: Found while capturing: /onboarding sets a cookie during render and shows "Eleva is having trouble" for a signed-in person who already has a membership, which is the invited-member path. Move the cookie write to a Route Handler or the proxy.

slices.title: Close the capture gaps
slices.scope: Extend the capture spec with what the panel could not see: cookie banner and preferences, open mega menus, the choose-how-to-meet step, slot-taken / hold-ended / payment-failed states, a booked member's home and session detail, the delete-account confirmation, and the video waiting room.

phases.title: From profile to paid booking
phases.goal: The path that earns revenue. A member always sees what she is booking, and the pay step feels safe.

slices.title: Quiet checkout frame
slices.scope: Replace the marketing header and footer in the funnel with logo, language, help and a secure-booking mark. One shared layout for every funnel step.

slices.title: Confirm and pay
slices.scope: One order summary (who, what, when with time zone, price, discount, total today, dated cancellation line, who provides the session). Hold timer and three reassurance lines beside the pay button. Promo code and tax number become links inside the summary. Fixed total-and-pay bar on phones. Still Stripe Checkout Sessions with the Payment Element.

slices.title: Details step and lighter consents
slices.scope: Explain the health-data consent in one plain line where it is asked, keep it as its own unticked choice, and reduce the weight of the rest. Say the cancellation policy once. Move the optional AI and transcription choice out of the booking gate. Match sign-up wording. Urgent help becomes one quiet line under the note field and on the thank-you page.

slices.title: Time picker
slices.scope: Scannable days and times on a phone, the continue action in place from the start, clear time zone.

slices.title: Thank-you as an arrival, and the unhappy paths
slices.scope: What happens next, add to calendar, how to join, the dated cancellation deadline, and a clear Space invitation. Free sessions read as free. Designed states for slot taken, hold ended and payment failed.

phases.title: Trust in the person
phases.goal: A member can choose an expert with confidence from the card and the profile.

slices.title: Checked-registration proof
slices.scope: A proof block beside the expert's name (who checked, what, when) with a one-tap explanation, the same mark on explorer cards, and how experts are ordered made visible.

slices.title: Profile header and spine
slices.scope: Header that holds up without a photo, facts as scannable items, a structured about (profession, focus, approach, training, your first session), reassurance moved up from the FAQ, and an empty profile that offers a next step.

slices.title: Services and booking on the profile
slices.scope: Even service cards with one action each, a clearer availability card, and on phones a sticky bar that opens the picker with the next open time.

slices.title: Expert card and need-first explorer
slices.scope: Card with face or compact no-photo layout, profession and focus, languages, how you meet, next open time and price. Areas of care above the grid, fuller filters, honest few-results and no-results states, unbookable experts handled apart.

slices.title: Report a concern
slices.scope: A visible, calm way to report a problem with an expert or a session, from the profile and the session page.

phases.title: Homepage and marketing
phases.goal: A first-time visitor knows in ten seconds what Eleva is, sees real experts, and has a way in.

slices.title: Homepage first two screens
slices.scope: Rebuilt in direction E on 2026-11-23, with D3.2: the film with one question and one action, eight questions that lead to areas of care, three experts from the directory, how experts are checked, how booking works, advisors, five questions, a closing block. Built, not yet judged.

slices.title: Homepage proof and rhythm
slices.scope: Built with D3.1 on 2026-11-23: how experts are checked as its own band, advisors in one band after the experts and the steps, steps that show the product, a closing block. Member voice and numbers wait until they are true. Not yet judged.

slices.title: Become an expert
slices.scope: Lead with the offer, the fee as its own block with a worked example (finance confirms the numbers), real product screens, a peer, and the questions experts ask next.

slices.title: For clinics and About
slices.scope: Clinics: a conversation as the main action, said once. About: the founders' story told once, shorter on phones, ending on members.

phases.title: Expert activation
phases.goal: A health professional gets from sign-up to a profile sent for review without wondering where she is.

slices.title: The expert door
slices.scope: An expert sign-up variant that carries intent into setup, a visible "Offer care on Eleva" entry on the member Space, a type picker and name step that speak care, and one step counter.

slices.title: Setup, rebuilt
slices.scope: Full screen, one question per screen, profile-first order (about you, how you see members, first service, licence, payouts, invoices), a live profile preview, save and exit. Builds on the O1 to O10 prototypes in the PoC lab.

slices.title: Money, licence and the finish
slices.scope: Payouts step that names Stripe, what she needs and when she is paid. Invoicing without greyed-out options. Licence as its own step with an example and a timeline. A finish that celebrates and links to real next steps.

slices.title: Sign-in and sign-up polish
slices.scope: A trust line on phones, people in the brand panel, check-your-email screens with something to do, language, help and legal links, lighter fields.

phases.title: Dashboards
phases.goal: Each home page answers its question; the rest is consistent and works on a phone.

slices.title: Expert Today
slices.scope: Next-session card with Join, a "Needs you" list from real state (requests, payouts not set up, missing photo), money at a glance, share your profile, a setup and growth checklist.

slices.title: Member home and sessions
slices.scope: With a booking: her expert, Join, what to prepare. Without: a guided way to find the right expert and how a session works. Empty states that teach. Clear navigation with an inbox and a phone bar.

slices.title: Privacy and data controls
slices.scope: What she agreed to (dated) apart from optional choices (switches). Download and delete explained in plain words, with status and visible safeguards.

slices.title: Expert calendar and services
slices.scope: A calendar that shows today and has actions, usable on a phone. Services list with the actions experts use most. A service editor that is not six opaque tabs.

slices.title: Expert consistency pass
slices.scope: Members list with search, finance first-run that explains how money flows, navigation grouped the way an expert thinks, headers that do not collide, plain words instead of jargon, a profile editor with a sense of completeness. Member settings and notifications on phones.

slices.title: Connected calendars
slices.scope: One picker for where sessions go (writable calendars only), a conflicts card per account with switches, the main calendar checked and set by default after connecting, official Google Calendar and Outlook icons, and a plain-language permissions step before leaving for Google or Microsoft.

slices.title: Connected calendars: hierarchy and session reminder
slices.scope: Provider as the card title and the email once below it, 'Main calendar' instead of the email, every calendar listed, the destination switch shown on, subscribed feeds named by host, and a 'Reminder in your calendar' select beside where sessions go (stored with the destination, sent to Google and Outlook).

slices.title: One account home
slices.scope: Everything about the person in /account: Profile, Notifications, Security, Privacy, Workspaces, and Billing for practices only. Space settings and privacy redirect there. Notifications show only real choices. A settings hierarchy: headline, title, hint, popover.

slices.title: Calm consent: one line and Details
slices.scope: Each consent on Privacy shows its purpose and consequence in one line; health data and AI open a Details dialog with the bullets and the notice link.

phases.title: Trust centre and legal pages
phases.goal: Trust facts are scannable, and a policy can be read and acted on from a phone.

slices.title: Trust centre and policy layout
slices.scope: Trust centre opens with fact tiles before the documents. Legal pages get a plain-language summary, contents on phones, last updated, and a way to act on a right.

phases.title: Calm, end to end
phases.goal: Every page says one thing at a time: no labels above headlines, no features that are not live, no system words, background behind (i) or Details.

slices.title: No labels above headlines
slices.scope: Remove the eyebrow from every dashboard PageHeader (Space, practice, clinic, academy, admin) and drop the prop from @eleva/ui.

slices.title: Public profile, calmer
slices.scope: Remove 'How booking works', turn the service eyebrow into a meta line, put 'What we check' behind an (i), keep one 'registration checked' line.

slices.title: Checkout and thank-you, calmer
slices.scope: Consents keep their statement and one line, with how to withdraw and the notice in a Details dialog; no mechanics hints (country, promo); thank-you page says each thing once (calendar note behind an (i), no duplicate join note, a short Space invite).

slices.title: Member Space, calmer
slices.scope: Join shows only on a video session that can be joined (it was greyed out on in-person and phone sessions); one action per session card and the card opens the session; when joining opens is said once, with the time; Payments lists only money that moved, named after the session, with plain statuses; the waiting room keeps one instruction and one privacy line.

slices.title: Practice: only what is live, in plain words
slices.scope: Only the ways of invoicing that work today are offered (Moloni and an unlinkable TOConline are not shown, on Invoicing, in setup and on Integrations); no line about what is not active; an invoice row is named after its session, with one plain status and one action (Try again only for a real failure); private links, payouts and the calendar feed lose their system words (token, hash, 404, Reversal pending).

slices.title: Service editor, each question once
slices.scope: Remove the duplicate mode, languages and currency from Basics; merge Kind into Policies.

slices.title: Practice menu and home
slices.scope: Calendars under Integrations, Relationships into Members, no repeated shortcuts or stats, one licence-status sentence.

slices.title: Clinic and Academy without promises
slices.scope: Remove 'later release' and 'on the way' promises; 'experts on your team'.

phases.title: The public site, rethought
phases.goal: A visitor recognises Eleva with the logo covered, and every public page passes the seven-seat panel.

slices.title: A brand direction for the public site
slices.scope: Directions (palette with a role for each colour, type, imagery, shapes) shown on the real homepage, expert profile and pay step, side by side, and scored by a blind panel. The founder chooses. The choice becomes the tokens of apps/web first, so the dashboards do not change under it, and the brand book is corrected to match the code. State on 2026-11-23: five directions are built in the playground (apps/poc, /brand-lab). A to D were judged blind twice and D led at about 8.0; the founder then asked for more character and less reliance on type, and E, In her words, was built with the frontend-design skill. E is not judged. Waiting for the founder's choice.

slices.title: Checkout: one frame on a phone, and the last details
slices.scope: Every step shares one frame on a phone (a one-line summary that opens, and a fixed bar with that step's action). Promo code and tax number live in the summary. Nothing optional sits between the total and the pay button. A guest can correct her email and move or cancel from the thank-you page, once product and security agree how she is recognised.

slices.title: Content pages
slices.scope: Newsletter, podcast, community, evidence-based care, contact and the founders' story: captured first, then rewritten and rebuilt to the ten writing rules in voice-notes.md. Each shows the real thing (an issue, an episode, a reply time) or an honest empty state.

notCovered: Video call room and waiting room, emails, the help centre (apps/docs), admin, team and academy apps were not audited in this pass.
Open mega menus, the cookie banner and its preferences dialog, the choose-how-to-meet step, and error states (slot taken, hold ended, payment failed) were not captured; D0.3 adds them.
The demo member has no bookings, so a booked member's home, session detail and report were judged from source, not screens; D0.1 fixes that.
Dark mode and PT/ES layouts were not captured. Captures are English, light theme.
No accessibility tooling (axe, screen reader) was run; a11y notes come from looking at the captures.
Findings marked for legal review are design proposals. The panel did not give legal advice.
Mobbin had no women's-health marketplace and no clinician licence check; those references come from other domains and are used for structure only.
The content pages (newsletter, podcast, community, evidence-based care, contact, history) have references and judging criteria but no captures or findings yet; D8.3 captures them first.
The three brand directions are proposals from references. None has been tested with members, and the motion ideas have no reference behind them because stills cannot show motion.
